About the translation

The dashboard converts published coefficients into transparent scenario comparisons without re-estimating the model or changing the paper's substantive claims.

How the calculator works

Planned-event exposure enters the PPML model as ln(Event + 1). The outcome remains a non-negative crime count under a log-link conditional mean. This distinction matters: the result is an association in expected reported crime, not a percentage change in Crime + 1.

  • Event counts must be non-negative whole numbers.
  • The baseline and comparison counts are transformed separately.
  • Reported robust standard errors generate coefficient-based 95% intervals.
  • The incident difference applies the relative association to an illustrative baseline mean.

Exact formulas

ratio = (E₁ + 1) / (E₀ + 1)

crime multiplier = ratioβ

association (%) = 100 × (ratioβ − 1)

incident difference = μ₀ × (ratioβ − 1)

Interpretation boundaries

The tool is interpretive rather than predictive. It does not estimate causal effects, forecast realized crime, evaluate intervention effectiveness, or prescribe police deployment, private-security staffing, or resource allocation. The reported coefficients already reflect observed public- and private-safety responses embedded in the study period.
